outline.title: Abstract
outline.description: A concise summary of the survey paper, highlighting the rapid evolution of LLM security threats and defenses from 2023 to 2026. It will outline the shift from unimodal, static vulnerabilities to complex, multimodal, and agentic attack vectors across training and inference phases, summarizing key findings in data poisoning, adversarial attacks, prompt injection, and hallucinations.

outline.title: Introduction
outline.description: This section establishes the motivation and scope of the survey, contextualizing the explosive adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) alongside their expanding attack surface. It will detail the temporal evolution of the field between 2023 and 2026, noting the transition from identifying baseline vulnerabilities to a sophisticated, co-evolutionary arms race between attackers and defenders. The introduction will clearly state the paper's contributions, providing a roadmap for the subsequent sections covering training-time threats (poisoning), inference-time threats (adversarial attacks and prompt injection), model reliability (hallucinations), testing methodologies, and holistic defenses.

outline.title: Background and Preliminaries
outline.description: Provides the foundational knowledge necessary to understand the security vulnerabilities of modern foundation models. This section will define key LLM and MLLM architectural components, including alignment mechanisms like Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). It will formally introduce the threat model, distinguishing between training-time vulnerabilities (e.g., poisoning) and inference-time exploits (e.g., prompt injection, adversarial queries). Furthermore, it will categorize adversaries based on their access levels (white-box vs. black-box) and capabilities, setting the stage for the detailed threat analyses in the core body sections.

outline.title: Training-Time Threats: Data and Model Poisoning
outline.description: Examines the alarming evolution of data and model poisoning attacks from 2024 to 2025. The section will begin with the initial phase of benchmarking generative backdoors in open-source models like LLaMA-2, Mistral, and GPT-J, referencing foundational works such as [Chowdhury_2024_Breaking] and [Li_2024_Backdoorllm]. It will then trace the critical transition from unimodal text-based vulnerabilities to highly complex, multimodal, and embodied AI attack vectors. A major focus will be placed on the exploitation of alignment and retrieval mechanisms, specifically highlighting how the RLHF pipeline—traditionally viewed as a safety mechanism—has become a vector for sophisticated poisoning attacks.

outline.title: Inference-Time Threats I: Adversarial Attacks
outline.description: Analyzes the rapid evolution of adversarial attacks and defenses in LLMs and MLLMs between 2024 and 2026. This section will cover the initial identification of domain-specific vulnerabilities, specifically detailing how standard models deployed in high-stakes sectors like healthcare were manipulated using sensitive datasets such as MIMIC-III, as demonstrated by [Yang_2024_Adversarial]. It will explore the transition from these baseline vulnerabilities to a sophisticated, multi-faceted arms race characterized by advanced offensive weaponization. The discussion will also introduce early defensive strategies, such as the contrastive prompt tuning mechanism proposed by [Wang_2024_Advqdet] for detecting query-based black-box attacks.

outline.title: Inference-Time Threats II: Prompt Injection and Jailbreaking
outline.description: Focuses on the transformative evolution of prompt injection and jailbreak attacks during the 2025-2026 period. It will document the definitive shift from static, rule-based defenses to a dynamic, automated adversarial landscape. The section will detail how attackers successfully automated the discovery of adversarial prompts using techniques like modified Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG), Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) fuzzing, and genetic algorithms, referencing key works like [Zhan_2025_LLM, Wang_2025_LLM, Maloyan_2025_LLM]. It will highlight the alarming Attack Success Rates (ASR) of 50% to 71% achieved against state-of-the-art LLM agents, emphasizing the unique vulnerabilities introduced by agentic environments.

outline.title: Model Reliability and Output Integrity: LLM Hallucinations
outline.description: Explores the conceptual maturation of LLM hallucinations and factual consistency research from 2023 to 2026. The section will cover the shift from basic detection mechanisms to highly optimized, mechanistically informed frameworks. It will highlight the 2023 era of zero-shot inference-time methods, specifically detailing the introduction of ChainPoll [Friel_2023_LLM], which demonstrated how LLM-based polling and Chain-of-Thought prompting could drastically reduce inference costs while outperforming competitors. The narrative will then move into 2024 and beyond, discussing the realization that non-factual generations are not merely binary errors, but require nuanced, conceptually rich evaluation paradigms.

outline.title: Cross-Cutting Defenses and Mitigation Strategies
outline.description: Provides a holistic overview of defense mechanisms, tracing the evolution from early 'patchwork' security to integrated, dynamic systems. It will discuss the 2024 reliance on external stateful detection and prompt-level manipulations, such as the contrastive prompt tuning for black-box detection [Wang_2024_Advqdet]. The section will then explore the 2025-2026 bifurcation into extreme computational efficiency and dynamic, ensemble-based systems designed to counter automated prompt injection and jailbreaking. It will also cover self-policing mechanisms, detailing how LLMs are increasingly used as their own evaluators and defenders when equipped with rigorous prompting strategies.

outline.title: Testing Methodologies and Evaluation
outline.description: A critical, dedicated section synthesizing the benchmarks, datasets, metrics, and evaluation frameworks used across all security categories. It will cover the evolution of Attack Success Rate (ASR) metrics in prompt injection (e.g., measuring 50-71% success rates in agentic environments), the use of domain-specific datasets like MIMIC-III for adversarial testing [Yang_2024_Adversarial], and the frameworks used to evaluate generative backdoors in models like LLaMA-2 and Mistral [Chowdhury_2024_Breaking, Li_2024_Backdoorllm]. Furthermore, it will analyze the trade-offs between computational cost and efficacy in hallucination detection, referencing the inference cost optimizations of tools like ChainPoll [Friel_2023_LLM]. The section will highlight the critical need for standardized, dynamic evaluation tools that can keep pace with automated fuzzing and genetic algorithm-based attacks.

outline.title: Discussion and Open Challenges
outline.description: Synthesizes the overarching trends and identifies critical gaps in the current research landscape. This section will discuss the fundamental inadequacy of static defenses against co-evolutionary adversarial threats. It will highlight open challenges, including the expanding attack surface of multimodal and embodied AI systems, the inherent vulnerabilities of the RLHF pipeline, and the difficulty of securing autonomous LLM agents against automated fuzzing (MCTS, GCG). The discussion will propose future research directions, emphasizing the need for mechanistically informed interpretability and robust, mathematically verifiable safety guarantees.

outline.title: Conclusion
outline.description: Summarizes the core findings of the survey, reiterating the rapid transition of LLM security from isolated, unimodal vulnerabilities to a complex, automated arms race spanning 2023-2026. It will provide actionable, practical recommendations for researchers and practitioners, emphasizing the necessity of moving beyond bolted-on security wrappers toward fundamentally secure-by-design architectures and dynamic, ensemble-based evaluation frameworks.
